finding.claim: The /rss endpoint opens a user-supplied URL with URI.open and returns the first 400 bytes of the response. Because of that, an attacker can make the server fetch internal or cloud-metadata URLs and read the result. With Ruby versions before 3.0, open-uri's Kernel#open behaviour can also be reached. On any version, URI.open follows redirects and supports http, https and ftp.
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read (open-uri); response body is returned to the caller

trace.note: params[:u] is passed directly to URI.open, which performs the request and reads the body
The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is non-blind SSRF

finding.guards_checked: There is no scheme check, host allowlist, private-IP or loopback blocking, or redirect restriction on this path. Nothing else in the file filters params[:u]. The TRUSTED allowlist is only applied in /trusted, not in /rss.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unauthenticated query param params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read with no scheme or host validation, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:14 applies only to /trusted.
